newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea to cut reserve requirement ratio.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea to cut reserve requirement ratio.

text.p: The Bank of Korea said on Thursday it would lower the bank reserve requirement ratio to an average of 3.32 percent from 5.45 percent at present, effective February 23.
The central bank also said in a statement it would apply a two percent reserve requirement ratio to deposits with banks raised through certificates of deposit (CDs).
When taking into account CDs, the ratio -- the proportion of deposits that banks must place as reserves with the central bank -- will be an average of 3.13 percent, the statement said.
Money market analysts say the reserve ratio cut is expected to be followed by drops in bank lending rates.
The central bank plans to reduce its rediscount lending to commercial banks to absorb all the surplus liquidity caused by the reduced ratio, the statement said.
The bank expects 2.8 trillion won of funds to be supplied into the money market due to the reduced reserve ratio.
The statement also said, from February 17, it would scrap the limit on CD issuances by banks in line with the plan to apply the reserve requirement ratio on the certificates.

Currently, commercial banks are allowed to issue CDs worth up to 150 percent of their net worth while the limit is set at the higher of either 400 percent of net worth or 35 billion won for foreign bank branches in South Korea, the statement said.
